# Open Science {#open-science}

#### 2000 - 2003 · UC Santa Cruz, UC San Diego

::: {.chapter-intro}
The early 2000s produced three projects that redefined what open science software could be. None of them was trying to build a platform. One was racing a supercomputer. Two were trying to make sense of data that no existing tool could handle. All three became the field standard.
:::

---

## The UCSC Genome Browser: Three Days Before a Supercomputer {#ucsc-genome}

**The project:** UCSC Genome Browser
**Campus:** UC Santa Cruz
**Period:** Summer 2000
**Key figures:** Jim Kent (PhD student), David Haussler (faculty)

::: {.origin-story}
*Section in preparation.*
:::

### What it became

The UCSC Genome Browser [@kent2002genome] is the reference tool for genomic research worldwide. It hosts assemblies for hundreds of species, is updated continuously, and remains the first stop for any researcher navigating genomic data.

{{< on-campus ucsc-genome >}}

## EEGLAB: The Most-Cited Scientific Software You've Never Heard Of {#eeglab}

**The project:** EEGLAB
**Campus:** UC San Diego (Swartz Center for Computational Neuroscience)
**Period:** 1997 - 2001 (first developed at the Salk Institute; later at UC San Diego)
**Key figures:** Scott Makeig

::: {.origin-story}
*Section in preparation.*
:::

### What it became

EEGLAB is an open source environment for processing EEG and related electrophysiological signals. The 2004 paper that introduced it [@delorme2004eeglab] had about 26,800 citations in OpenAlex in November 2026 [@openalex2026eeglab].

{{< on-campus eeglab >}}

## Cytoscape: Mapping the Cell {#cytoscape}

**The project:** Cytoscape
**Campus:** UC San Diego, with the Institute for Systems Biology (Seattle) and the Whitehead Institute
**Period:** 2003
**Key figures:** Trey Ideker and collaborators

::: {.origin-story}
*Section in preparation.*
:::

### What it became

Cytoscape [@shannon2003cytoscape] is a widely used platform for network biology. Researchers use it to visualize disease pathways, protein interactions, and molecular networks. Its developers reported over 300,000 downloads a year in 2025 [@ono2025cytoscape].

{{< on-campus cytoscape >}}
